name: Continuous device, address, and payment assurance

attribution.legal_posture: Source-qualified investigative reporting and defensive abstraction; named-person attribution, nationality finding, and adjudicated legal fact remain unestablished.

caveats: Limit collection to necessary employment and security data with documented retention and access controls.
Named vendor investigators and multi-source reporting support the control, while individual indicators remain nonspecific.
A single address, country, payment service, remote-work request, or BYOD choice is contextual; DPRK affiliation requires corroborated evidence.

statements: Organizations should reverify identity and work location when material facts change, correlate shipping and device custody with endpoint telemetry, and review unexpected payment-routing or address changes together with other evidence.
limitations: Named vendor investigators and multi-source reporting support the control, while individual indicators remain nonspecific.
No single address, country, payment service, remote-work request, or BYOD choice proves DPRK affiliation.
Limit collection to necessary employment and security data with documented retention and access controls.

statements: Use this behavior or governance pattern only with corroborated, consistently applied human review.
limitations: No single accent, ethnicity, nationality, appearance, camera or audio quality, geography, address, payment service, remote-work preference, device-hosting request, or technical-answer anomaly establishes fraud or DPRK attribution.
Do not publish or derive legal identities, pseudonyms, stolen identities, victim details, private selectors, leaked communications, credentials, or image matches from these records.

lazarus_group_routes: existing continuous re-verification and endpoint chain-of-custody controls
